OpusCast for **Windows** and **macOS**: the same app as on Linux, now on Windows 10/11 and on Macs with macOS 12 Monterey or newer, Intel and Apple silicon.

## Windows

Download **OpusCast-v1.1-Windows-Setup.exe** below (or the .zip to run it without installing).

- Windows SmartScreen will say it protected your PC: choose *More info* → *Run anyway* (the app isn't signed with a paid certificate).
- When Windows asks whether OpusCast may use the network, allow it on *Private networks*, so the TV can fetch the videos.
- Right-click a video, song or photo → *Open with* → *OpusCast*.

## macOS

Download **OpusCast-v1.1-macOS.dmg** below and drag OpusCast to Applications. One app for Intel and Apple silicon Macs, macOS 12 Monterey or newer.

- The app isn't signed by Apple, so the first time: right-click it → *Open* → *Open* (macOS 12–14), or on macOS 15 open it once, then System Settings → Privacy & Security → *Open Anyway*.
- To cast the desktop, allow OpusCast under *Screen Recording* when macOS asks, then start it again.
- macOS doesn't hand the Mac's sound to apps. To send it to the TV too, install [BlackHole](https://existential.audio/blackhole/) (free) and choose it as the output.

## In both

Everything the Linux app does, with ffmpeg built in:

- **Videos** with subtitles (files next to the video and tracks inside it, switched while the video plays on Samsung TVs), resume where you left off, and *Show on PC*: a muted copy of the video in the window, in step with the TV.
- **Music:** songs or whole folders one after another, with title, artist, album and cover on the TV. Formats the TV doesn't list (often Opus or Ogg) are converted to MP3 first.
- **Photos:** a slideshow; pick one photo to flip through its folder. HEIC, WebP, rotated and huge photos are converted on the way.
- **Cast the desktop:** the screen (and on Windows its sound) live on the TV, 720p or 1080p, 30 or 60 frames a second, any screen.
- Works with more TVs than Samsung (LG, Sony, Philips, Hisense, Panasonic, Android TV sets): OpusCast uses each TV's own names for the formats it plays, retries while a TV is busy and seeks the way it accepts. Philips: turn on *Digital Media Renderer – DMR* if the TV isn't found.
- The Skynet intro (off by default), English and Slovak.

Linux: songs picked together now play in album order. Android: unchanged since 1.0 (the APK is attached again).
